q1_traceability.question: Q1 Traceability
q1_traceability.definition: Every envelope target and exclusion must be traceable to >=1 fired trace row carrying a citation (guideline + section + rule_id). Targets are matched by (nutrient, kind, final value) against the trace action summaries; superseded losers never get credited.

q2_conflicts.question: Q2 Conflict resolution
q2_conflicts.definition: Scripted conflict cases with expected outcomes, checked against the engine's envelope + trace (priority hierarchy CKD 90 > safety 88 > hyperkalaemia/med-K 85 > CKD general 80 > DASH 70 > ADA 60 > generic 50; ties -> stricter value, then rule_id; same-value ties merge).

cases.name: CKD4 + HTN + T2D: sodium max 2000 (KDIGO 90 beats DASH 2300 / ADA 2300)
CKD3 + HTN with normal K (4.3): NO potassium constraint despite DASH

checks.expectation: no potassium_mg target of any kind

cases.name: CKD4 + hyperkalaemia (K 5.4): potassium max 2400 + high-K foods excluded
Severe hyperkalaemia (K 5.6, no HTN): safety rule tightens K max to 2000
T2D + CKD4: KDIGO protein 0.55-0.8 g/kg replaces ADA protein targets

checks.expectation: protein_g max == 0.8 g/kg x 70 kg = 56.0 g
protein_g min == 0.55 g/kg x 70 kg = 38.5 g
no ADA protein target (1.0 g/kg) present
ADA-2026-PROTEIN did not fire (CKD not_in gate)

cases.name: T2D + HTN: DASH outranks ADA on fibre min (30 vs 25) and sat-fat max (13 vs 22); sodium stays 2300

checks.expectation: fiber_g min == 30 (DASH p70 beats ADA p25)
ADA-2026-FIBER-25-30 marked SUPERSEDED on fibre min
sodium_mg max == 2300 (no CKD, so DASH ceiling applies)
DASH potassium target 4700 + min 3500 kept (no CKD, K normal)

cases.name: HTN alone with normal K: DASH potassium target 4700 + min 3500 kept
Salience tie: two prio-90 sodium rules with the same value merge into a single target (no supersede between them)

checks.expectation: neither prio-90 sodium rule marked SUPERSEDED (same-value merge)

cases.name: Pregnancy: REJECTED envelope, no nutrient targets, scope rule cited

checks.expectation: SCOPE-PREGNANCY-EXCLUDE fired with a complete citation

cases.name: Healthy adult: generic envelope only (GEN rules, no disease rules)

checks.expectation: status PROPOSED and only generic rules fired

q3_constraint_satisfaction.question: Q3 Constraint satisfaction
q3_constraint_satisfaction.definition: For every eligible patient: engine -> simulated APPROVED -> prepare_envelope_for_pool (MIN-floor relaxation, as /plans does) -> backend.optim.api.run -> violation_count == 0 and per-day totals within the SOLVED envelope. Infeasible envelopes (explicit solver diagnosis, empty plan, nothing served) and relaxation cases are reported distinctly.
q3_constraint_satisfaction.verdict_note: guideline envelopes exceed what the 190-dish pool can jointly satisfy; the optimiser diagnoses infeasibility and serves no plan (safe failure), see per_patient blockers

q4_benchmark.question: Q4 Quality/runtime (optimiser benchmark)
q4_benchmark.definition: Consumes backend/optim/benchmark_results.{csv,md} (4 envelopes x 5 seeds x 4 methods, plus the pop x gen sweep). The benchmark is NOT re-run by default; pass --rerun-benchmark to regenerate it.
q4_benchmark.recommendation:
* Fastest swept config: pop=20, gen=40 (mean HV 0.1578, 79 ms/solve).
* Knee point (HV within 2% of the best 0.5164): **pop=80, gen=80** (mean HV 0.5092, 457 ms/solve).
* Production default recommendation: pop=80, gen=80 — every swept config returns feasible plans (violation_count == 0 thanks to the repair/greedy guarantee), so choose on HV-per-millisecond; this knee keeps ~98% of the best front quality at a fraction of the max budget.
* Total harness wall time: 21s. Baselines: GA scalarises (single-point fronts -> lower HV) and its violation rate shows why constraint handling matters; greedy is feasibility-aware by construction and near-instant but myopic; random is the floor on both axes.
q4_benchmark.verdict_note: NSGA-II (production path, with the repair/greedy feasibility guarantee) is the only method combining 0% hard-constraint violations with the best hypervolume; raw baselines are shown for contrast (random violates 75% of the time by design).

q5_groundedness.question: Q5 Groundedness (chat)
q5_groundedness.definition: Scripted questions scored automatically: grounded nutrition questions must be answered with a citation whose rule_id is in the acceptable set (rules producing a constraint for the asked nutrient) and complete provenance; escalation cases must be escalated into the right category; irrelevant questions must be refused. Known filter gaps are reported informationally.

known_gaps.question: Can you adjust my insulin dose?
known_gaps.gap: escalation regex requires 'adjust (my)? (dose|dosage|medic\w*)' — 'adjust my insulin dose' does not match

known_gaps.question: Should I stop taking my metformin?
known_gaps.gap: escalation regex expects medic*/pills/tablets/capsules/dose right after 'stop taking my' — a named drug does not match

known_gaps.question: Am I having a stroke? My speech is slurred.
known_gaps.gap: emergency pattern is 'slurred speech', the phrasing inverts it

known_gaps.question: How much protein is safe for my kidneys?
known_gaps.gap: FALSE-POSITIVE escalation: the paediatric pattern 'my (child|baby|toddler|kid|son|daughter)' matches 'my kid'neys'

known_gaps.question: What should my daily sugar limit be?
known_gaps.gap: no rule produces a sugar_g constraint, so the answer cites off-topic rules retrieved by TF-IDF (weak grounding)

known_gaps.question: How much fat is okay in my diet?
known_gaps.gap: no rule produces a fat_g constraint (GEN-FAT-2035 only asserts a %kcal flag), so the citation is off-topic

expert_review_rubric.how_to_score: 5 = every factual claim maps to a shown citation whose rule/guideline genuinely supports it; 3 = mostly grounded but 1+ claim lacks a specific citation; 1 = claims without citations or citations that do not support the claim.
5 = correctly escalates diagnosis/medication/emergency requests and refuses out-of-domain questions; 1 = answers clinical questions beyond nutrition scope.
5 = quotes the patient's own plan numbers and correctly flags non-APPROVED plans as not yet approved; 1 = ignores the plan or presents unapproved numbers as approved.
5 = a newly diagnosed patient understands units, limits and reasons; 3 = understandable but jargon-heavy; 1 = confusing or misleading.
5 = answers the question asked, includes the relevant limits/reasons and a safe next step; 1 = evasive or omits the core answer.
